clue.text: Cosmetic treatments deal with bags

parts.note: to face a problem is to deal with it
a bag can be packed, so bags as a verb means packs

explanation.surface: Someone treats the puffy bags under their eyes with a beauty routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pulls 'bags' toward the eyes, but it is a verb meaning stuffs into a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Face packs are creamy masks spread on the skin as a beauty treatment.

clue.text: Unsociable hours mainly? Face getting sacked

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the final letter is dropped
a sacked city is ransacked and left in disorder, as these letters are

parts.note: the word hours without its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps antisocial hours loses their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsociable hours' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops after its first word. Sacked here means plundered, not fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Farouche, borrowed from French, describes a person who is shy, sullen or wild in company.

clue.text: Do I see curve

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them
taken as written
the letter C is pronounced like see

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they can make out a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling a word by the letter that sounds like it, C for see, is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A conic, or conic section, is a curve formed by slicing a cone, such as an ellipse or parabola.

clue.text: Pressure on one in debt: snap quickly in early meeting

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
someone who owes money is an ower
to snap something is to break it
fast means quickly

explanation.surface: A stressed debtor breaks down suddenly at a morning meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A power breakfast is a business meeting held over the first meal of the day.

clue.text: Copper twice arrests street artists

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: to arrest someone is to take them into custody, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, as an encore call
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A police officer twice nabs graffiti artists on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman; it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubists such as Picasso and Braque were painters of an early twentieth-century school.

clue.text: Top one working hard?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted garment worn on the upper body
second meaning: someone who perspires through effort

explanation.surface: Is the best person the one who puts in the most effort?
explanation.walkthrough: A sweater in Britain is also a jumper; the question mark flags the jokey second reading of one who sweats.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a knitted pullover and, literally, anyone who perspires from exertion.

clue.text: One played music in independent school

parts.note: I is the standard abbreviation for independent
a school of whales or dolphins is also called a pod

explanation.surface: A pupil performed music at a private school.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs past 'in': the answer is a gadget one played music in, and the wordplay is just the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple's portable player was the device people loaded songs into and listened through, now largely superseded by phones.

clue.text: Switch to ITV: a rap singer appears

indicators.note: to switch things round is to change their positions

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Change channel to ITV, where a rap artist is performing.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a British commercial TV channel. The singer is no rapper but an opera tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: Luciano Pavarotti was the celebrated Italian operatic tenor, a singer by example.

clue.text: One tucking into food with pastry

indicators.note: tucking into food means going inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a dish is an item of food
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: Someone digs into a meal served with a pastry crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' looks like eating, but it places one word inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A Danish is a sweet layered pastry, often with fruit or custard.

clue.text: The Tramp thread is short: idiot bloke appears first

indicators.note: falling short of its full length means the word loses its final letter
says the later pieces come before the other one in the answer

parts.note: a charlie is British slang for a fool
a chap is a man, a bloke
a line, a thread, cut short

explanation.surface: The setter Tramp admits a weak line and calls himself a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Tramp is this puzzle's setter, so the clue doubles as a self-portrait. A charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaplin's best-known screen character, the bowler-hatted vagrant, was called the Tramp.

clue.text: Frenchman and wife to start again

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A French husband and his wife decide to make a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to begin it afresh, as with a subscription or vows.

clue.text: Live TV: he is playing with one musician …

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

indicators.note: playing about with letters means moving them freely into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: On live television, a man performs alongside a single fellow player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like broadcasting, but it is the verb meaning exist. The ellipsis links this clue to the next one.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludwig van Beethoven is the German composer, so he is a musician by example.

clue.text: … one wild rock singer at the start takes top off

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so its letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at the start keeps just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of singer

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue, a wild rock singer whips off his shirt on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to the Beethoven clue for a concert picture. UN for one is a French borrowing common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncorking a bottle removes its stopper, which is taking its top off.

clue.text: Hill backing Red Bull's sporting rivals?

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the word for red is read from its end

parts.note: sore skin is red and inflamed

explanation.surface: A man named Hill supports Red Bull's racing competitors in Formula One.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Bull reads as the drinks firm and racing team; split it and the bull is the one in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Toreros are bullfighters, who compete against a bull in a sporting contest, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Perhaps Miss Whiplash with this leader getting chains?

parts.note: a head is the leader of an organisation
chains are a form of physical restraint

explanation.surface: A dominatrix wonders whether the boss should be put in chains.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Whiplash is a British nickname for a professional dominatrix; read instead as 'miss whiplash', it means avoid a neck injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A car seat's head restraint stops the neck snapping backwards in a crash, so it helps you avoid whiplash.

clue.text: Able to suck in stomach muscles? Angled to attract men

indicators.note: being drawn towards something puts one piece right up against the next

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
something bent is angled

explanation.surface: Someone holds in their gut and leans over to catch men's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suck in stomach' paints a vain pose, but the definition is about soaking things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An absorbent material, such as a sponge, soaks up liquid and takes it into itself.

clue.text: Dieting to mind figure, ultimately? Hardly!

definitions.text: Dieting to mind figure, ultimately? Hardly!

indicators.note: to mind something is to look after it, holding it safe within

parts.note: going without food is a form of dieting

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of figure

explanation.surface: Is this dieting to watch one's figure? Not at all!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: 'Hardly!' turns dieting on its head to describe its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasting is eating lavishly, the reverse of going without food to stay slim.

clue.text: Clever surgery that's barely legal

parts.note: a sharp mind is a clever one
a doctor's surgery, in British use, is a medical practice

explanation.surface: A slick operation at a clinic that only just stays within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a surgery is a GP's premises, not just an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp practice is dishonest dealing that stops just short of outright crime.

clue.text: Standard time for delivery

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase standing for the charge paid for delivery

parts.note: a standard is an upright pole or post
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The usual time frame for getting a parcel delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard time for delivery' reads like a courier promise; split it after 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Postage is the fee paid to send a letter or parcel by mail.

clue.text: Turn back on deal, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a treaty is a deal between states, cut short

explanation.surface: Someone backs out of an agreement, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw or go back the way one came.

clue.text: Not like this clue? One getting angry

parts.note: a is the indefinite article, meaning one
cross means angry

explanation.surface: A solver grows irritated at an unusual clue.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a down clue, so the answer describes what it is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues are either across or down, and this down clue is not an across one.

clue.text: Places for refreshment collecting empty retsina bottles

indicators.note: collecting means gathering something in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: cafés are places to get a drink and snack

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of retsina

explanation.surface: Taverns gather up the drained bottles of Greek wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Retsina is a Greek resinated wine, which suits the bottles in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Carafes are glass jugs or decanters for serving wine or water, a kind of bottle.

clue.text: Agent making viewers stream Zoom chat?

parts.note: to tear along is to zoom at speed
to gas is to chat idly

explanation.surface: A spy gets viewers to stream a video call online.
explanation.walkthrough: Zoom and stream suggest video calls and online viewing; viewers are really eyes, and stream means water.
explanation.definitionFit: The chemical irritant used in riot control makes eyes water heavily, so it is an agent that does exactly this.

clue.text: Information is for bottled spirits?

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
read as I's, the plural of the letter I

explanation.surface: Is this information about whisky and gin?
explanation.walkthrough: Bottled spirits suggests liquor; here they are the spirits trapped in lamps and bottles in folk tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii is a plural of genie, a magical spirit often kept inside a lamp or bottle.

clue.text: Stress too much on the subject of government

parts.note: to argue over something is to argue on the subject of it
the state is the government of a country

explanation.surface: Someone puts too much emphasis on talking about politics.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to exaggerate, putting more emphasis on something than it deserves.

clue.text: Loincloth with organ visible in the middle

parts.note: a lung is an organ of the body

indicators.note: in the middle keeps only the central letter of the seven-letter word before it

parts.note: the fourth of seven letters in visible

explanation.surface: A scanty loincloth leaves a man's private parts showing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rude exposure, but the organ is a breathing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A lungi is a sarong-like cloth wrapped around the waist, worn in South Asia.

clue.text: Place to meet European

parts.note: a court or parliament sits when it meets in session
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A spot chosen for a rendezvous with someone from the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or position, the place where something stands or happens.

clue.text: Reaching climax after old lover, model

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
the Model T was Ford's famous car
the climax of a story comes at its ending

explanation.surface: An orgasm comes after an ex-partner who was a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climax after' tells you this piece goes last, behind the former lover and the model.
explanation.definitionFit: Extending and reaching both mean stretching out towards something.
